mission: Quantify the class of days where NO armed setup fires a signal, using 2026-07-10 (SPY +$7 off the low, zero armed setup firing after 11:33 ET, 734 HOLDs) as the exhibit.

frozen_rules_applied_in_priority_order: 1. FLUSH_RECOVER / SPIKE_FADE -- an early (first 25% of bars) >=0.6% move from the open that reclaims/fades 61.8%-138.2% of itself by the close (round-trips, does not extend into a fresh trend).

2. FLUSH_TREND_DOWN / FLUSH_TREND_UP -- a FAST early break (extreme within the first 25% of bars, >=0.6% from open) that reclaims <61.8% and the day still closes >=0.3% net in the break's direction (never meaningfully recovers).

3. TREND_UP / TREND_DOWN -- an 'anchored' move >=0.6% with <35% max giveback of the move-so-far at any point after the anchor. The anchor is the OPEN, unless the session low (for up) / high (for down) was set in the first 25% of bars AND is beyond the open -- then the anchor is that early extreme, so a day that flushes early and then grinds the rest of the way (07-10's shape) is correctly read as a trend 'off the low', not a flush.
4. GAP_GO / GAP_FADE -- |opening gap vs prior RTH close| >=0.3%, resolved (net move same-sign = GO, opposite-sign = FADE) with |net move| >=0.3%.
6. CHOP -- catch-all: directional but with >=35% retrace, or a wider range that never cleanly resolves into trend/flush/gap/range.
day_shape_taxonomy.note: Every session gets exactly ONE label (first matching rule wins). Thresholds were calibrated once against known days (2026-07-10, 2026-06-30) then frozen before running the full 30-day pass -- not re-tuned after seeing the answer.

definitions.fired: core setups (ribbon_ride): the 'setup' field is non-null on a tick (scoring passed), independent of what verdict/gate follows. extra setups: extra_signals[i].fired == true.
definitions.entered: core setups: verdict in {ENTER_BEAR, ENTER_BULL}. extra setups: extra_exec[i].action == 'PLACED'.
definitions.orders/placed: exec.status == 'PLACED' (core) or extra_exec[i].action == 'PLACED' (extra). NOTE: verdict ENTER_* does NOT guarantee a real order attempt -- see the 'action' field, which can downgrade an ENTER_BULL verdict to a no-op (e.g. SKIP_STALE_TRIGGER) with no exec dispatch at all. This audit reports verdict-level and action-level counts SEPARATELY rather than conflating them.
definitions.fills: NOT reliably reconstructable from core-decisions.jsonl alone (exec.status 'PLACED' means order-submitted, not fill-confirmed, and is frequently absent even on real ENTER_* rows). journal/trades.csv is the fill-of-record for the two core accounts AND the separate fleet-arm accounts, cross-checked selectively below where it changes the conclusion.

2026-07-10.narrative: Open 752.05 -> early low 748.10 -> ground up to a 755.42 high, closed 754.86 (+0.37% net from open, but +0.90% off the early low with only 33% max giveback -- TREND_UP by the frozen rule). BULLISH_RECLAIM_RIDE_THE_RIBBON (Safe account) scored SUPER-tier ENTER_BULL five times at the open (09:31-09:35 ET, spy=751.55) -- but the action taken was SKIP_STALE_TRIGGER every time: the trigger bar was 2026-07-09T15:55 (the PRIOR session's last bar), so the engine correctly refused to act on a carried-over trigger. Bold account then scored the same SUPER-tier setup six more times (11:21-11:33 ET) but all six hit SKIP_MIN_PREMIUM_FLOOR. From 11:21-12:55 ET the setup kept re-scoring (bull_score=11 throughout) but every tick was blocked: SKIP_BULL_1100_1200 (a deliberate lunch-hour block, 11:21-11:33) then SKIP_ELITE_BULL_LEVEL_RECLAIM (11:51-12:55, 20 occurrences that day) -- a gate that requires a FRESH named level to re-enter on. After 12:55:04 ET the setup field went null for the rest of the session: the tape never offered another trendline_rejection/level_reclaim trigger, so ribbon_ride had NOTHING left to score against through the 12:55->15:55 close, during which SPY still ran from 753.81 to a 755.42 high / 754.86 close (further $1.05-$1.61 of continuation with zero engine engagement). bollinger_squeeze also fired 13 ticks that day (last at 15:10:03 ET, genuinely mid-afternoon) but its 4 'PLACED' extra_exec actions all timestamp to 00:54-01:01 ET (before the open, not RTH) -- a separate logging anomaly, not confirmed afternoon coverage (flagged, not relied on). VERIFIED: zero rows on 2026-07-10 (780 ticks, both accounts) show a non-empty exit_pass -- no position was EVER open that day. Net result: 42 fired ticks, 11 scored ENTER_BULL verdicts, ZERO real order attempts converted, ZERO fills, entire $7.32-range session.
2026-07-10.correction_to_mission_framing: 'Not one armed setup even fired a signal after 11:33' is not quite accurate -- BULLISH_RECLAIM_RIDE_THE_RIBBON fired/scored through 12:55 ET (42 ticks, 11 ENTER_BULL verdicts), and bollinger_squeeze fired through 15:10 ET. The real, verified failure is sharper: EVERY scored ENTER_BULL was blocked before a real order (stale-trigger + premium-floor), and after 12:55 the setup stopped scoring ANYTHING for the rest of the day because the tape stopped offering a fresh level-retest -- the 734 HOLD figure is confirmed correct (734 of 780 ticks), and 504 of those 734 HOLDs landed after 11:33 ET.

flag_pullback_continuation.why_this_is_the_hole_fix: Its trigger grammar (volume impulse + shallow VWAP-proximity pullback) is STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT from ribbon_ride's grammar (trendline_rejection / level_reclaim / confluence, all keyed off DRAWN chart levels). On 2026-07-10 and 2026-06-30, ribbon_ride's bull side scored repeatedly but had no fresh drawn level to trigger a re-entry on -- a pattern that needs no named level at all (just impulse + VWAP-relative pullback) is the natural complement, not a retuned copy of the same idea.

corrections_to_the_original_framing: 'SPY trended $7 off the low' is precisely confirmed: low $748.10 -> close $754.86 = $6.76, high $755.42 -> $7.32 range. Matches to the dollar.
'734 HOLDs' is precisely confirmed (734 of 780 ticks on 2026-07-10 were HOLD).

'Not one armed setup even fired a signal after 11:33' is NOT precisely accurate -- BULLISH_RECLAIM_RIDE_THE_RIBBON scored through 12:55 ET (11 ENTER_BULL verdicts total that day) and bollinger_squeeze fired through 15:10 ET. The verified, sharper failure: every scored ENTER_BULL was blocked before a real order attempt, and after 12:55 ET literally nothing scored for the rest of the session.

The hypothesis 'sustained TREND days = biggest hole' is DIRECTIONALLY supported but the dollar-opportunity ranking (frequency x uncaptured-$) does NOT put TREND_UP/DOWN in first place over the 30-day window -- GAP days are both MORE frequent (8/30 vs 4/30) and carry more aggregate $ range ($98.69 vs $29.85) in this sample. TREND_UP's real distinguishing signature is not raw frequency or $ range, it's a CONSISTENT, VERIFIED mechanism (see below), not primarily a size argument.

The hypothesis 'FLUSH days without prior levels = second hole (the C21 class)' is NOT supported by the 2 FLUSH_TREND_DOWN days with data in this window (2026-06-25, 2026-07-07) -- BOTH show real BEARISH_REJECTION_RIDE_THE_RIBBON participation, and 2026-07-07 has 7 real fills in journal/trades.csv. Sample is thin (n=2) so this is a correction of degree, not a full kill -- but the data does not back the hypothesis as stated.

The real, best-evidenced headline is narrower and better-corroborated than either original hypothesis: on EVERY session in this window where BULLISH_RECLAIM_RIDE_THE_RIBBON sustained high scoring against a persistently-bullish tape (2026-06-29, 06-30, 07-09, 07-10 -- 4 of 4), SKIP_ELITE_BULL_LEVEL_RECLAIM was the dominant or exclusive blocker (4, 64, 104, and 20 occurrences respectively; 270 total across the 11-session window, the single largest non-HOLD verdict in the whole dataset). This is a KNOWN, ALREADY-AUDITED gate (2026-06-30 bull-unblock thread, commit 79f842c): unblocking it was tested and found NET NEGATIVE (-$241, cohort WR 14.3%) -- so this hole is not fixable by loosening the EXISTING setup's gates. The one lever that COULD catch a smooth grind independently (sequence_reclaim) is confirmed STRUCTURALLY COUPLED OFF in filters.py (can only fire as a redundant co-trigger, never standalone) per the same audit thread -- filed, not fixed, low priority per that thread's own verdict. The fix has to be a structurally different detector, not a gate tweak: flag_pullback_continuation.
